Take the pan off the heat and slowly whisk in the 4 cups of milk. Let it cool a little. This is enough honey milk for 4 lattes; keep the rest in the fridge.
Fit the Double basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to ESPRESSO.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place a 12 oz mug under the spout and press START BREW.
Pour 1 cup of the honey milk (up to the LATTE line) into the milk jug. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until DAIRY lights up, turn the froth dial to THIN FROTH and press START FROTH.
Pour the honey milk into the espresso and finish with a drizzle of honey.
recipes.adaptation: Starbucks combines the warm honey milk with the espresso, then froths more milk on top. Frothing the honey milk itself does both in one step.
recipes.blurb: A latte made with honey cooked until it turns caramel, then stirred into steamed milk.

recipes.name: Maple Pecan Latte
steps: Fit the Double basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to ESPRESSO.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Put the maple syrup in a 12 oz mug.
Place a 12 oz mug under the spout and press START BREW.
Pour 1 cup cold milk (up to the LATTE line) into the milk jug. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until DAIRY lights up, turn the froth dial to THIN FROTH and press START FROTH.
Stir the maple syrup into the espresso, add the milk and stir again.
Top with whipped cream and the chopped pecans.
recipes.adaptation: Stephanie uses a 1.5 oz shot. A Double basket shot is about 2 oz.
recipes.blurb: Espresso and steamed milk with maple syrup, topped with whipped cream and chopped pecans.

recipes.name: Café con Leche
ingredients: Double shot of espresso (dark Cuban-style roast if you have it)
steps: Pour ½ cup cold whole milk (fill to the minimum line if needed) into the milk jug. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until DAIRY lights up, turn the froth dial to STEAMED MILK and press START FROTH.
Pour the hot milk into an 8 oz mug and stir in the sugar.
Fit the Double basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to ESPRESSO.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place a small cup under the spout and press START BREW.
Pour the espresso into the milk and stir until light brown. Taste, and add more sugar or a tiny pinch of salt if you like.
recipes.adaptation: Ericka brews ¼ cup of moka-pot coffee. A Double basket shot is close to that, and STEAMED MILK replaces heating the milk in a pan.
recipes.blurb: The Spanish and Cuban breakfast coffee: strong espresso with hot milk and a little sugar.

recipes.name: Iced Mocha
ingredients: 1 tbsp simple syrup or chocolate syrup
¼ cup (2 oz) milk or oat milk
steps: Put the chocolate chips in a heatproof jar.
Fit the Double basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to ESPRESSO.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place the jar under the spout and press START BREW.
Cover the jar and shake hard until the chocolate melts. Pour into a 12 oz glass full of ice.
Pour the milk and simple syrup (fill to the minimum line if needed) into the milk jug. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until DAIRY (or PLANT-BASED) lights up, turn the froth dial to COLD FOAM and press START FROTH.
Spoon the foamy milk over the chocolate espresso.
recipes.adaptation: This one is brewed on ESPRESSO, not COLD-PRESSED: the hot shot is what melts the chocolate. Sonja shakes the milk in a jar to foam it; the COLD FOAM preset does it for you.
recipes.blurb: Espresso and chocolate over ice with a splash of milk. A chocolate iced latte.

recipes.name: Iced White Chocolate Mocha
ingredients: Cold foam: 2 oz heavy cream + 1 oz milk
steps: Put the white chocolate chips in a heatproof jar.
Fit the Double basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to ESPRESSO.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place the jar under the spout and press START BREW.
Cover and shake hard until the chocolate melts. Stir in the 2 tbsp milk and pour into a 12 oz glass full of ice.
Pour the heavy cream and milk into the milk jug. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until DAIRY lights up, turn the froth dial to COLD FOAM and press START FROTH.
Spoon the cold foam over the top.
recipes.adaptation: Brewed on ESPRESSO so the hot shot melts the white chocolate.
recipes.blurb: Espresso and melted white chocolate over ice, topped with a cold foam.

recipes.name: Iced Lavender Oat Milk Latte
ingredients: Double shot of cold-pressed espresso (2 oz)
steps: Fit the Double basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to COLD-PRESSED.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Put the lavender syrup in a 16 oz glass.
Place a 16 oz glass under the spout and press START BREW.
Stir, fill the glass with ice and top with the oat milk.
recipes.adaptation: Sues makes a lavender sugar powder and uses blonde espresso; her notes say lavender syrup works too. Use a lighter roast if you have one.

subRecipes.name: Lavender syrup
steps: Bring the sugar, water and lavender to a simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Turn off the heat, let it steep 20 minutes, then strain into a jar. Keeps in the fridge for about a month.

recipes.blurb: Cold-pressed espresso with lavender syrup and oat milk over ice. Floral and creamy.

recipes.name: Iced Pistachio Latte
ingredients: Double shot of cold-pressed espresso (2 oz)
6 oz cold milk or plant milk
steps: Fit the Double basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to COLD-PRESSED.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Fill a tall glass with ice.
Place the glass under the spout and press START BREW.
Stir in the pistachio syrup, pour in the cold milk and top with chopped pistachios.

subRecipes.name: Pistachio syrup
steps: Lightly crush the pistachios in a small pan, add the water and sugar and bring to a boil.
Simmer 5 minutes, stirring now and then, then strain out the nuts and cool. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

recipes.blurb: Cold-pressed espresso with pistachio syrup and cold milk over ice, topped with toasted pistachios.

recipes.name: Iced Dirty Matcha Latte
ingredients: Double shot of cold-pressed espresso (2 oz)
steps: Sift the matcha into a small bowl.
Place a small cup under the hot water spout.
Press HOT WATER, set the temperature to LOW and the size to the smallest size, then press START.
Whisk 2 tbsp of the hot water into the matcha until smooth, then whisk in the vanilla syrup or honey.
Pour the matcha into a clear 12 oz glass, fill with ice and slowly pour the milk over an ice cube so it layers on top.
Fit the Double basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to COLD-PRESSED.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place a small cup under the spout and press START BREW.
Slowly pour the espresso over an ice cube to make a third layer. Stir before drinking.
recipes.blurb: An iced matcha latte with a shot of espresso poured on top. Green tea and coffee in layers.

recipes.name: Toasted Vanilla Oat Milk Shaken Espresso
ingredients: Triple shot of cold-pressed espresso (3 oz, light roast if you have it)
steps: Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to COLD-PRESSED.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Put the toasted vanilla syrup and a handful of ice in a cocktail shaker.
Place a cocktail shaker under the spout and press START BREW.
Shake hard for about 20 seconds until frothy.
Pour into a 16 oz glass of ice and top with the oat milk.
recipes.adaptation: Sues uses 3 oz of espresso. The Luxe basket's cold-pressed shot is about that size.

subRecipes.name: Toasted vanilla syrup
steps: Split the vanilla bean, cut it into small pieces and toast them in a dry pan over medium-low heat for a few minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Bring the water and sugar to a boil, lower the heat, add the vanilla and simmer about 10 minutes.
Cool, keeping the vanilla pieces in to infuse. Strain before using.

recipes.blurb: Three shots of cold-pressed espresso shaken with toasted vanilla syrup and ice, topped with oat milk.

recipes.name: Iced Chocolate Almond Milk Shaken Espresso
ingredients: 1½ tbsp chocolate syrup, plus a drizzle
1 cup ice, plus more for the glass
steps: Fit the Double basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to COLD-PRESSED.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Put the chocolate syrup and 1 cup ice in a cocktail shaker.
Place a cocktail shaker under the spout and press START BREW.
Shake hard until frothy and ice cold.
Strain into a glass full of ice, add the almond milk and drizzle with chocolate syrup.
recipes.blurb: Cold-pressed espresso shaken with chocolate syrup and ice, topped with almond milk.

recipes.name: Vanilla Iced Coffee
ingredients: ¼ cup (2 oz) milk of your choice
steps: Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to OVER ICE and press SIZE until 6 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Fill a 12 oz glass with ice and add the vanilla syrup.
Place the glass under the spout and press START BREW.
Add the milk, stir and taste. Add more syrup or milk if you like.
recipes.adaptation: Sonja uses ½ cup cold brew concentrate or strong coffee. OVER ICE brews it strong and hot straight onto the ice.

subRecipes.name: Vanilla syrup
steps: Warm the sugar and water in a small pan over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Don't let it simmer.
Take it off the heat, stir in the vanilla and let it cool. Keeps in the fridge for about a month.

recipes.blurb: Iced coffee sweetened with vanilla syrup and a splash of milk.

recipes.name: Brown Sugar Iced Coffee
steps: Put the brown sugar in a 12 oz glass, add 2 tbsp hot water from the hot water spout and stir until dissolved.
Add the ice and slowly pour in the milk.
Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to OVER ICE and press SIZE until 6 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place the glass under the spout and press START BREW.
Stir before drinking.
recipes.adaptation: Coffee at Three uses ⅓ cup of cold brew or double-strength coffee. The 6 oz OVER ICE size gives a slightly bigger, equally strong drink.
recipes.blurb: Iced coffee sweetened with a quick brown sugar syrup and topped with milk.

recipes.name: Iced Coffee Float
ingredients: Up to ½ cup (4 oz) milk
steps: Fit the Double basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to COLD-PRESSED.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND. The built-in scale doses by weight.
Pull the tamping lever down firmly twice, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Fill a tall heatproof glass with ice and add syrup if you like.
Place the glass under the spout and press START BREW.
Pour in the milk, leaving room at the top.
Float a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top and serve with a long spoon.
recipes.adaptation: Elaine brews hot espresso over the ice. COLD-PRESSED is smoother over ice and melts the ice cream less.
recipes.blurb: Espresso and milk over ice with a scoop of vanilla ice cream floating on top. A coffee dessert drink.

recipes.name: Chocolate Cream Cold Brew
ingredients: Chocolate cream: 2 oz heavy cream, 1 oz 2% milk, 1 tbsp chocolate syrup, ½ tsp malt powder, 1 tsp sugar, tiny pinch of salt
steps: Pour the heavy cream and milk into the milk jug, then add the chocolate syrup, malt powder, sugar and salt. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until DAIRY lights up, turn the froth dial to COLD FOAM and press START FROTH.
Keep the chocolate foam in the jug while you brew.
Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to COLD BREW and press SIZE until 8 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Fill a 16 oz glass halfway with ice and add the vanilla syrup.
Place the glass under the spout and press START BREW.
Pour the chocolate cream foam over the top.
recipes.adaptation: Stephanie blends a bigger batch of the foam (½ cup cream, ½ cup milk). This is half of it, sized for the frother.
recipes.blurb: Vanilla cold brew topped with a malty chocolate cold foam.

recipes.name: Irish Cream Cold Brew
ingredients: ½ oz (1 tbsp) Irish cream syrup
Cold foam: ½ cup heavy cream, 1 tbsp Irish cream liqueur or syrup, 1 tbsp sugar
steps: Pour ½ cup cold heavy cream into the milk jug, then add the Irish cream liqueur (or syrup) and sugar. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until DAIRY lights up, turn the froth dial to COLD FOAM and press START FROTH.
Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to COLD BREW and press SIZE until 10 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Fill a 12 oz glass with ice.
Place the glass under the spout and press START BREW.
Stir in the Irish cream syrup to taste, leaving an inch at the top.
Spoon the foam over the top.

subRecipes.name: Irish cream syrup (alcohol-free option)
steps: Heat the sugar and water until dissolved, then turn off the heat.
Whisk in the cocoa and espresso powder, then the vanilla and whiskey.
Strain into a jar. Keeps a month in the fridge.

recipes.blurb: Cold brew with Irish cream syrup and an Irish cream cold foam. Alcohol is optional.

recipes.name: Brown Sugar Cold Brew with Brown Sugar Foam
ingredients: ¼ cup sweetened vanilla oat or almond milk, chilled
steps: Pour the chilled vanilla oat or almond milk (fill to the minimum line if needed) into the milk jug, then add the dark brown sugar. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until PLANT-BASED lights up, turn the froth dial to COLD FOAM and press START FROTH.
Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to COLD BREW and press SIZE until 10 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Fill a 16 oz glass with ice and add the brown sugar syrup.
Place the glass under the spout and press START BREW.
Spoon the foam on top and dust with cinnamon sugar.
recipes.adaptation: Sunny steeps a pitcher of cold brew overnight. The Pro's COLD BREW style makes one glass in minutes.

subRecipes.name: Brown sugar syrup
ingredients: ½ cup packed dark brown sugar
steps: Simmer the brown sugar and water, stirring, until dissolved and slightly thick.
Cool before using. Keeps in the fridge for about 2 weeks.

recipes.blurb: Cold brew with brown sugar syrup, topped with a brown sugar oat milk foam and cinnamon sugar.

recipes.name: Sweet & Spiced Gingerbread Coffee
ingredients: 2 tsp brown sugar, plus a sprinkle
⅛ tsp ground cinnamon, plus a sprinkle
steps: Put the molasses, brown sugar and cinnamon in a 12 oz mug.
Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to CLASSIC and press SIZE until 8 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place the mug under the spout and press START BREW.
Stir until the molasses dissolves.
Pour 4 oz cold whole milk (fill to the minimum line if needed) into the milk jug. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until DAIRY lights up, turn the froth dial to THICK FROTH and press START FROTH.
Pour the frothed milk over the coffee and sprinkle with cinnamon and brown sugar.
recipes.adaptation: Starbucks uses gingerbread-flavored pods. Plain beans work fine: the molasses and spice carry the flavor.
recipes.blurb: Brewed coffee with molasses, brown sugar and cinnamon plus steamed milk. Tastes like gingerbread.

recipes.name: Maple Vanilla Brown Sugar Coffee
steps: Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to CLASSIC and press SIZE until 8 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place a 12 oz mug under the spout and press START BREW.
Stir in the half-and-half, brown sugar, vanilla and maple syrup.
Top with whipped cream and a pinch of cinnamon if you like.
recipes.adaptation: Starbucks brews maple pecan flavored pods. With regular beans, the teaspoon of maple syrup brings the maple back.
recipes.blurb: Brewed coffee with brown sugar, vanilla, a little maple and half-and-half.

recipes.name: Hot Buttered Coffee
steps: Put 1 tbsp of the spiced butter mix in a 10 oz mug.
Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to RICH and press SIZE until 8 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place the mug under the spout and press START BREW.
Stir until the butter melts. Add a cinnamon stick and whipped cream if you like.
recipes.adaptation: Taste of Home calls for a dark roast, so we brew on RICH. Keep it in the Classic list since it's an everyday mug.

subRecipes.name: Spiced butter mix (makes 20)
steps: Mix everything until smooth.
Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.blurb: Dark coffee stirred with a spiced butter and brown sugar mix. Rich and cozy, like hot buttered rum.

recipes.name: Spiced Coffee
ingredients: 1 small drop anise extract (about ⅛ tsp, or to taste)
steps: Put the sugar, chocolate syrup, anise, cinnamon stick and cloves in a 12 oz mug.
Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to CLASSIC and press SIZE until 8 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place the mug under the spout and press START BREW.
Stir and let it steep 3 to 4 minutes, then lift out the cloves. Keep the cinnamon stick in as a stirrer.
recipes.adaptation: Taste of Home slow-cooks 8 cups for 2 hours. This is one mug, steeped right in the cup.
recipes.blurb: Coffee steeped with cinnamon, cloves and a hint of anise, sweetened with sugar and chocolate syrup.

recipes.name: Peppermint Mocha
ingredients: Whipped cream and crushed candy canes
steps: Put the chopped chocolate in a 14 oz mug.
Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to RICH and press SIZE until 8 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place the mug under the spout and press START BREW.
Stir until the chocolate melts.
Pour ½ cup cold milk (fill to the minimum line if needed) into the milk jug. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until DAIRY lights up, turn the froth dial to STEAMED MILK and press START FROTH.
Stir the milk and peppermint extract into the mug. Top with whipped cream and crushed candy canes.
recipes.adaptation: Gemma simmers everything in a pan for 2 minutes. Hot RICH coffee melts the chocolate and STEAMED MILK heats the milk.
recipes.blurb: Coffee with melted dark chocolate, milk and peppermint, topped with whipped cream and crushed candy canes.

recipes.name: Maple Cream Coffee
steps: Pour the half-and-half (fill to the minimum line if needed) into the milk jug, then add the maple syrup. Set the jug on the frothing platform with the whisk inside.
Press MILK TYPE until DAIRY lights up, turn the froth dial to STEAMED MILK and press START FROTH.
Pour the warm maple cream into a 10 oz mug.
Fit the Luxe basket into the portafilter, put the dosing funnel on and set it in the grinding cradle.
Turn the center dial to RICH and press SIZE until 6 oz lights up.
Turn the grind dial to the number Barista Assist recommends, then press START GRIND.
Give the portafilter a gentle shake to level the grounds, then lift off the funnel.
Lock the portafilter into the brew head.
Place the mug under the spout and press START BREW.
Stir and top with whipped cream.
recipes.adaptation: Taste of Home warms the cream and syrup in a pan and makes 2 cups. This is one cup.
recipes.blurb: Rich coffee with maple syrup and creamy half-and-half, topped with whipped cream.
